description:
FILED s518d (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-17) from #3284 (Scalar-List-Utils t/uniqnum.t ran 20 of 23, rc 255).  LOUD, pre-existing.

`my $x = EXPR for LIST;` -- a declaration with a `for` statement modifier -- dies at run time "PCL: statement not supported ... -- Bug. Fell through. Missing case: ['Token::Magic<$_>', ... funcall]".

REPRODUCER (scratch/s518d/pr/myfor.pl):
    my @n = (1, 2);
    my $dummy = sprintf "%d", $_ for @n;
    print "ok ", (defined $dummy ? "d" : "u"), "\n";
perl 5.40.3: `ok u` (the `my` is scoped to the modifier's statement; the outer $dummy is a fresh undef).  PCL: the die above.
uniqnum.t line 301 (`my $dummy = sprintf "%d", $_ for @nums;`) is that statement; rows 21-23 sit behind it.


=== DONE (s522a, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-19..20) ===
FIXED in commit 9d49f1a8 (rebased; was 2b6ae75c).  A `my` statement with a LOOP modifier (for / foreach / while / until) went to v1, which dropped it.  `_decl_loop_modifier` (Pl/Parser2.pm) re-parses the statement's own text as `for (LIST) { my DECL = EXPR }` (line-aligned) and lowers it through the ordinary compound lowering; the declaration then lowers once more with no init, so the variable is a fresh undef after the loop, as perl's pad clearing makes it.  `if` / `unless` on a `my` is a compile error in modern perl: out of scope (principle 9).  ir-spec updated.
Probes: the reproducer `ok u`, `$_` ranges, list / array / hash decls, the `while` counter, a side-effecting EXPR counted N times, inside a sub called twice, the `foreach` spelling -- all = perl.
Bars: SLU uniqnum.t runs to its plan (18/5, the 5 already blessed); its *PLAN* row left cpan-board14-fails.tsv by edit; guard rows in Pl/t/parser2-02.t (the runtime row fails on aff112d7); gate PASS 324 files / 11,090 rows on the rebased tree 055ebe2e (MAIN-READY-37 + the batch); sweep clean 18,759; corpus-diff IDENTICAL.
